agree.reason: The update is candid about the bad quarter, but the reader is cold about the skipped updates and gets only a generic apology and "from now on you will," with no January 7 date and no offer of monthly numbers. The 6 clinics already committed to the new product are also left out, so a sceptical investor has little to hold on to.

honest.reason: No numbers are invented and the runway and no-show claims check out. But the claim that clinics "we've lost" can still buy reminders is speculation. It also leaves out the two customers on the same records system, paying $3,800 a month, so the risk looks smaller than the writer knew it to be.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out about 11 months of runway, "close to half" of no-shows gone, and that MRR would have grown without the one loss. It never states the growth in dollars (about $5,500), and it gives no figure for the 6 committed reminder buyers.

right_comparison.reason: The update never says what happens if nothing changes: it doesn't name a cash-out month, and it doesn't mention the $3,800 a month at similar risk of leaving. That makes the status-quo path look milder than the facts show.

qualification.reason: "Within the next quarter we'll decide whether to cut burn or prepare to raise" gives no threshold of reminder sales, no date, and no consequence the investor could check.

objections.reason: It meets the obvious worries about a flat quarter and the lost chain. It handles the investor's real complaint, being left in the dark, weakly: it gives no reason for the silence and no dated commitment. It also doesn't ask for the specific 20-minute call.

fit.reason: It is in the right format for an investor email, but it runs past 500 words. It also leaves [Company] and [Your name] as placeholders when the names were known, and says "next month" instead of December 1.
